packages.rig: n/a
packages.contents: READ FROM THE FILES (operator downloaded 2026-09-13 03:14, extracted without importing): 75 files, 14.2 MB of which 13.9 MB is the PDF manual. THE "3D" IS THIN: two tilted world-space uGUI canvases (Canvas_DefaultTemplate1 / MobileTemplate1) and a camera Animator that blends between TWO poses - UIMenuManager.cs Position1()/Position2() set one float "Animate" to 0/1 over MenuCamPos1/MenuCamPos2, plus a MenuCamIdle drift. 10 C# scripts (UIMenuManager, UISettingsManager, theme editor), TextMeshPro SDF atlases for Lato/Poppins/Rubik, 3 click SFX + a music sample, panel/button/cursor PNGs. Depends on com.unity.postprocessing 2.3.0, textmeshpro 3.0.6, ugui.
we_would_use: REFERENCE ONLY, and a thin one: a menu as panels placed in 3D with a camera that moves between stations. BootStage3D already drives a camera with two out-of-phase drift cycles (47 s orbit, 31 s rise), which is more than this pack does
the fonts are free Google Fonts (Lato, Poppins, Rubik) if ever wanted - the SDF atlases themselves are Unity TextMeshPro data and do not port
packages.godot_cost: Nothing ports (uGUI, C#, TMP atlases, Unity post-processing).
packages.on_record: roadmap now: FREE, in the operator account, operator asked for the download
packages.reason: Free and on the operator theme (3D scenes instead of text-heavy menus), but reading the files shows the idea is two camera poses behind flat panels. The 3D menu we want - a live room with stations - is BootStage3D grown, not this pack.
